notes: A music video no longer goes quiet at about fifty-seven seconds and leaves the ordinary song playing under it. The sound a sharp picture plays is a copy of the film in its own right, so its own length is read the moment it knows it: when that copy is shorter than the film, the tab stops trusting it instead of finding out a minute later.

When the answer has the same film as a single file, that copy becomes the picture itself - one file, its own sound, from the same second - so the whole film plays with the whole sound at once instead of two copies fighting over one of them.
When there is no such copy, the song takes the sound at once and the line under the picture says why, instead of the film playing on in silence until the cut runs out.

A film that runs out long before the song is now looked past: the next result for that song is tried before the song takes the tab, so a cut teaser no longer leaves the tab frozen on its last frame while the ordinary audio plays.

The check on how long a video really is now happens whenever the video says its length, not only at the first moment it loads - a length that arrived a moment late used to skip the check altogether, which is how a fifty-seven second file played to its end before.
